title: Multiplying and Dividing Decimals
seo_title: Multiplying and Dividing Decimals – Primary 4 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Multiply and divide decimals by 1-digit numbers; multiply and divide by 10, 100 and 1,000; convert fractions with denominators 10, 100 and 1,000 to decimals. (summary of the NERDC Primary 4 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 4 maths worksheets on multiplying and dividing decimals by 1-digit numbers and by 10, 100 and 1,000, and changing tenths, hundredths and thousandths to decimals. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Multiply a decimal as if it were a whole number, then put the same number of decimal places in the answer.
  • Divide as usual and put the decimal point in the answer straight above the decimal point in the number.
  • × 10, × 100, × 1,000 move the digits 1, 2, 3 places to the left; ÷ 10, ÷ 100, ÷ 1,000 move them to the right.

Examples

Example

2.45 × 3

245 × 3 = 735

2 decimal places

Answer: 7.35

Example

4.6 ÷ 100

Move 2 places right

Answer: 0.046

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Losing the decimal pointCount the decimal places in the question.
Moving the digits the wrong wayMultiplying makes the number bigger.
Writing 3/100 as 0.33/100 = 0.03.

faq.q: Why does × 10 make a number bigger?
faq.a: Each digit becomes worth ten times as much.
